citation.note: Prohibit using employee's prior salary to set new pay; enforce pay-secrecy ban on employer policies (CRS § 8-5-103).

body.context: setting compensation for a promotion or base-pay change

citation.note: Payroll records (wages, deductions, statements, hours) retained at least 3 years; selection and promotion records for employment duration plus 3 years (EPEWA); personnel records 5 years for CADA defense (CRS § 8-4-103).

Paid leave: 48 hours paid sick leave per year (HFWA, CRS § 8-13.3-401 et seq.), plus 12 weeks paid family/medical leave if eligible under Colorado FAMLI (CRS § 8-13.3-501 et seq.; 0.88% premium, $184,500 cap in 2026).

body.interaction_rule: Paid leave: 48 hours paid sick leave per year (HFWA, CRS § 8-13.3-401 et seq.), plus 12 weeks paid family/medical leave if eligible under Colorado FAMLI (CRS § 8-13.3-501 et seq.; 0.88% premium, $184,500 cap in 2026).

citation.note: Wages payable at least monthly; monthly pay periods payable within 10 business days of period end (CRS §§ 8-4-102–103).

Final pay on involuntary termination due immediately (within 6 hours of the next business day if payroll is closed); resignation pays on the next regular payday; accrued vacation payout within 14 days of written demand; willful violations risk treble damages (CRS §§ 8-4-109, 8-4-105).

body.deadline_description: Final pay on involuntary termination due immediately (within 6 hours of the next business day if payroll is closed); resignation pays on the next regular payday; accrued vacation payout within 14 days of written demand; willful violations risk treble damages (CRS §§ 8-4-109, 8-4-105).

citation.note: EPEWA posting and notice duties (CRS §§ 8-5-101–102): postings carry pay range, benefits description and close date; pre-selection promotion notice to similarly situated employees; post-selection notice within 30 days.

body.required_disclosure: EPEWA posting and notice duties (CRS §§ 8-5-101–102): postings carry pay range, benefits description and close date; pre-selection promotion notice to similarly situated employees; post-selection notice within 30 days.

citation.note: Non-competes void unless the employee earns at or above the highly compensated worker threshold (amount to verify per SB 25-083) and the restriction is no broader than necessary to protect trade secrets; physician covenants void (CRS § 8-2-113).

body.rule: Non-competes void unless the employee earns at or above the highly compensated worker threshold (amount to verify per SB 25-083) and the restriction is no broader than necessary to protect trade secrets; physician covenants void (CRS § 8-2-113).

citation.note: WARN Act: No Colorado mini-WARN act.

body.note: WARN Act: No Colorado mini-WARN act.

citation.note: Minimum wage $15.16/hour statewide as of 2026-01-01; Denver $19.29/hour and other local floors attach as locality-level overlays; tipped cash minimum $12.14/hour with tips to the state minimum (CRS § 8-6-102).
Equal pay for substantially similar work regardless of sex; all employers with Colorado employees covered; maintain posting, wage-history and selection records (CRS § 8-5-101 et seq.).
Itemized pay statement each payday: gross pay, each deduction with reason, net pay, pay period dates and rates; retainable paper or electronic format (CRS § 8-4-103).

Independent contractor test (CRS § 8-6-101 et seq.): modified ABC test requiring both control-freedom and independent-trade engagement, with no usual-course prong; employer bears the burden; nine statutory factors.

body.test_description: Independent contractor test (CRS § 8-6-101 et seq.): modified ABC test requiring both control-freedom and independent-trade engagement, with no usual-course prong; employer bears the burden; nine statutory factors.

citation.note: Employee access to personnel file: employers must permit inspection and copying of the employee's own file once per calendar year without unreasonable delay; reasonable copying costs (CRS § 8-2-129).

CADA retaliation bar (CRS § 24-34-402): no discharge, demotion, pay cut or schedule change for discrimination complaints, CCRD charges or participation; wage-claim activity likewise protected; NDAs cannot silence unlawful-conduct reporting (POWR Act).
Written separation notice (SB 22-234, CRS § 8-90-107): every terminated employee receives UI-eligibility and reason notice at or before separation.

citation.section: (statutory section not stated in the research file)
citation.note: Drug testing: No state rule prohibiting private-employer drug testing; federal requirements and best practices apply.
Breach notification (CRS § 6-1-716): notify affected individuals of personal-information breaches without unreasonable delay or at latest 30 days after discovery, by mail, email or telephone.

AI hiring decisions (Colorado AI Act, SB 24-205, effective 2026-02-01 to verify): high-risk employment decisions (hiring, compensation, promotion, termination) need impact assessments, documentation, employee notice and human-review rights.

Biometric data (HB 24-1130, effective 2025-07-01): informed written consent before collection, a written retention/deletion policy, and destruction by the earliest of purpose-fulfilled, 24 months after last interaction, or 45 days after retention is unnecessary.
